newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end slightly higher, thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end slightly higher, thin volume.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly higher in shallow Monday trade as investors were restrained by a lack of sellers, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index closed 0.17 points higher at 559.40, supported by gains in Hatton National Bank which rose five rupees to 200. Commercial Bank rose one rupee to 100 rupees.

Local institutions focused their attention on some 10 firms either because of good earnings prospects or sharp share price falls recently, Shanil Perera of brokerage Lanka Securities said. They included John Keells Holdings and Sampath Bank.
"The problem is to find sellers," Perera said, adding sellers quoted too high prices after the index showed firm support at 550 points.

"We are looking at primary opportunities because the low level of share liquidity drives up prices," Manjula de Silva of CTC Eagle Fund Management said, referring to rights or other new issues. Turnover was a thin 16.2 million rupees.

After the market closed, the government said Sri Lanka's August consumer price index, based on a 12-month moving average, rose 13.9 percent year-on-year against 4.8 percent rise a year earlier. -- Prithi Kodagoda 941-434319
